newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet investors approve Rambaud for board.
newsitem.headline: Eramet investors approve Rambaud for board.

text.p: Shareholders of Eramet confirmed Yves Rambaud as a board member of the French nickel producer at the annual meeting on Thursday amid expectations he would be confirmed as chairman by the board.

The previous conservative government had wanted to replace Rambaud after he objected to the planned transfer of a mining licence on the Pacific territory of New Caledonia from Eramet to a nickel smelter joint venture held by local Kanak interests and Falconbridge of Canada.

"Yves Rambaud was re-elected at the AGM to the board. We hope he will be re-elected as chairman at the next board meeting, which will be held this afternoon," Eramet Director Alain Ray told Reuters after the annual general meeting.
State holding company ERAP, which owns 55 percent of Eramet, had wanted a few months ago to oust Rambaud over the New Caledonia dispute but minority shareholders and employees opposed that move.

Rambaud welcomed the new Socialist government's decision to commission an independent report, due in September, on the construction of a nickel smelter in northern New Caledonia. The subject was one of the differences between the company and the government.
The report "should lead to a more general review of the best way to make the most of New Caledonia's mining reserves," Ray said.
"This new measure seems essential to us. It should allow us to find a realistic approach to this problem, in the interest of all New Caledonians," he said.

The board also put a number of resolutions to the shareholders on the "functioning and composition of the board" at the request of minority shareholders, which included several large U.S. investment funds, he said.

Eramet expects first-half net profits for 1997 to be at least as high as those a year ago, Rambaud told shareholders. The 1997 half-time results will include its 46 percent stake in manganese company Comilog, which was not included the 1996 results. It has since raised its Comilog holding to 61 percent.
The company reported on Wednesday first half sales down 4.6 percent at 2.02 billion francs.
